issues.t: Second gear can overheat and break inside the automatic transmission
issues.sym: Slipping, a flashing D light, harsh or delayed shifts, or the SUV suddenly losing drive or locking up.
issues.why: Early five-speed automatics had poor lubrication to the second-gear clutch, so it could overheat and fail. Acura recalled these SUVs to add an oil jet kit and update the software.
issues.next: Check the VIN for completion of recall 04V176. If the transmission slips or the D light flashes, stop driving and have it inspected before it fails completely.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping, shudder or failure
issues.sym: Shudder around 30-40 mph, slipping between gears, hard shifts or the transmission no longer going into gear.
issues.why: The five-speed automatic in the first-generation MDX has a long record of clutch and torque converter wear, even after the early-model fixes.
issues.next: Change the fluid with genuine Honda fluid and have any slipping or shudder checked right away. A badly slipping unit usually needs a rebuild or replacement.

issues.t: Power steering pump whine and leaks
issues.sym: Whining or buzzing when turning, especially on cold mornings, heavy steering at first, or fluid drips near the pump.
issues.why: The power steering pump is a frequent replacement part on the MDX. It can suck in air through a worn inlet seal or hose and wear out quickly when fluid runs low.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and look for leaks. Have the inlet seal, hoses or pump replaced before the pump runs dry.

issues.t: Key can come out of the ignition when not in Park
issues.sym: The key can be pulled out while the shifter is not fully in Park, and the parked SUV may roll away.
issues.why: The ignition interlock lever could deform over time, so the key no longer stayed locked in until the shifter was in Park. Acura recalled these SUVs.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 12V573. Until it is fixed, always confirm the shifter is in Park and set the parking brake.

issues.t: Air bags may go off without a crash
issues.sym: An air bag warning light, or in rare cases an air bag deploying while driving with no crash.
issues.why: A fault in the air bag control unit could set off the air bags unexpectedly. Acura recalled the 2003 MDX to replace the unit.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 15V045 and get it done right away if it is open.

issues.t: Stability control can apply the brakes on its own
issues.sym: The SUV pulls or slows without you pressing the brake, sometimes with stability control or ABS lights.
issues.why: A fault in the vehicle stability assist module could apply individual brakes unexpectedly. Acura recalled these model years.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 13V092 and have it done before driving much further.

issues.t: Battery drain from the Hands Free Link module
issues.sym: A dead battery after the SUV sits overnight or for a few days, sometimes with Bluetooth phone calls not working.
issues.why: The Bluetooth Hands Free Link module can stay awake after the SUV is shut off and slowly drain the battery. A revised module was released.
issues.next: If the battery keeps dying, have a shop test for a parasitic drain and check the HFL module before replacing the battery or alternator.

issues.t: Side mirror motor noise or failure
issues.sym: Grinding or clicking when adjusting the side mirrors, mirrors that won't move, or mirror memory settings no longer working.
issues.why: The motor and gears inside the power mirror actuators wear out and are a common repair on this SUV.
issues.next: Have the mirror actuator replaced. It is not a safety issue unless the mirror can't be aimed properly.

issues.t: A/C works on and off or battery drains from A/C relay
issues.sym: Air conditioning that blows warm air at times, or a battery that drains overnight.
issues.why: The A/C compressor clutch relay can stick, either cutting out the A/C or keeping the clutch powered after shut-off.
issues.next: Have the A/C relay tested. It is a cheap, easy part to replace.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: Oil level dropping between changes, a low-oil warning, blue smoke or fouled spark plugs and misfires.
issues.why: The piston rings on the 3.7L V6 can clog with carbon and stop controlling oil, so the engine burns oil.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every fill-up and top up as needed. Ask a dealer for an oil consumption test and whether any coverage applies.

issues.t: Active damper shocks wear out
issues.sym: Knocking or a bouncy, floaty ride, sometimes with a suspension warning on models with the active damper system.
issues.why: The electronically controlled shocks on Advance-package models can fail and are expensive to replace.
issues.next: Have the dampers inspected. Some owners switch to conventional shocks when they fail.

issues.t: Torque converter shudder at cruising speeds
issues.sym: A vibration or shudder like driving over rumble strips at roughly 20-60 mph, or hesitation when accelerating.
issues.why: The torque converter lock-up clutch can judder as the fluid wears. Acura issued a bulletin calling for fresh fluid and, on 2014 models, a software update.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to apply service bulletin 16-044 (fluid flush). Get it fixed early so the converter isn't damaged.

issues.t: Driveshaft bolts may loosen on AWD models
issues.sym: Clunking or vibration from under the SUV, or loss of drive if the driveshaft comes loose.
issues.why: Some all-wheel-drive models built in mid-to-late 2013 had driveshaft bolts at the transfer case that weren't tightened properly. Acura recalled them.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 13V571. If you hear clunking from underneath, stop driving and have it towed in.

issues.t: Rear subframe can rust through
issues.sym: Clunks from the rear, a wandering or unstable rear end, or visible heavy rust on the rear subframe.
issues.why: In salt-belt states the rear subframe can corrode where the suspension mounts, and a part could separate. Acura recalled MDXs registered in affected Northeastern and Midwestern states.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 26V365. If the rear feels loose or clunks over bumps, have it inspected before driving further.

issues.t: Tailgate lights fail from water getting in
issues.sym: Bulb-out warnings, or brake, tail or turn lights on the tailgate not working.
issues.why: Water can get into the tailgate light housings and wiring, corroding the connections. Acura recalled these SUVs and later expanded the fix.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 19V256 and 25V259. Have dead rear lights fixed promptly so other drivers can see you brake.

issues.t: Rough or jerky shifts from the 9-speed automatic
issues.sym: Jerky low-speed shifts, a delay before the SUV moves, clunky upshifts, or hesitation when accelerating.
issues.why: The nine-speed automatic introduced for 2016 was known for unrefined shifting. Acura released software updates and a bulletin for harsh upshifts.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check for transmission software updates, including bulletin B20-015, and confirm they were done.

issues.t: Connecting rod bearing failure
issues.sym: Knocking from the engine, rough running, warning lights, loss of power or the engine stalling.
issues.why: Some crankshafts were not machined correctly, which can wear out the rod bearings and seize the engine. Acura recalled affected SUVs, and federal regulators later opened an investigation into failures in this engine.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 23V751. If you hear knocking, stop driving and have the SUV towed to a dealer.

issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and stall the engine
issues.sym: Rough running, check engine light, hard starting, or the engine stalling while driving.
issues.why: Several recalls cover fuel pumps that can lose performance; on later models the in-tank pump's impeller can swell and jam.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 19V060, 21V215 and 23V858 and get the free pump replacement. If the engine stalls, steer to safety and call for a tow.

issues.t: Engine doesn't restart after Auto Idle Stop
issues.sym: The engine shuts off at a light as designed but fails to restart, or an Idle Stop unavailable message appears.
issues.why: Restart logic and engine conditions could prevent a reliable restart. Acura released new engine software and extended warranty coverage for idle-stop repairs.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about bulletins B23-001 and B23-002. You can switch Idle Stop off with its button until the update is done.

issues.t: Collision braking system brakes for no reason
issues.sym: The collision warning goes off or the SUV brakes hard on its own with nothing in the way.
issues.why: The radar and camera system can misread objects such as overpasses or parked cars. Acura sent dealers repeated repair guidance for unexpected braking events.
issues.next: Have a dealer check for software updates and sensor alignment. Keep the front sensor and windshield camera area clean.

issues.t: Timing belt teeth can separate
issues.sym: Engine noise, a check engine light, or the engine suddenly stalling and not restarting.
issues.why: Some timing belts were made with a defect that let the teeth peel away from the belt, which can stop the engine. Acura recalled them.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 19V298 and get the belt replaced right away if it's open.

issues.t: Check engine light from a sticking purge valve
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0441, usually with no change in how the SUV drives.
issues.why: The evaporative system's purge control valve can stick intermittently. Acura issued a bulletin to replace it.
issues.next: Have the code read and ask the dealer about bulletin B23-035.

issues.t: Passenger seat sensor can crack and set off air bags
issues.sym: An air bag warning light or an incorrect passenger air bag status light; in rare cases the air bags can deploy without a crash.
issues.why: The weight sensor under the front passenger seat can crack and short out. A 2024 recall was expanded in 2026 to cover more model years.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 24V064 and 26V332 and have the sensor replaced as soon as possible.

issues.t: Type S engine can stall from fuel injection software error
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power or the engine stalling, sometimes with warning lights.
issues.why: A software error in the fuel injection control unit on Type S models could shut down the engine. Acura recalled them for a software update.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 25V031. If the engine loses power, get to a safe spot and have the update done before regular driving.

issues.t: Power steering assist can cut out
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy, often with a steering warning light.
issues.why: Electric power steering software could put the system into a failsafe mode and stop giving assist. Acura recalled these SUVs.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 26V721. If steering becomes heavy, slow down carefully and get the software update before driving much.

issues.t: Brake pedal pivot pin may not be secured
issues.sym: A brake pedal that feels loose, sits at an odd angle or shifts when pressed.
issues.why: The pin the brake pedal pivots on may not have been locked in place at the factory, so the pedal can move out of position. Acura recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 25V391 and have it fixed before driving if the pedal feels unusual.

issues.t: Center screen can go blank and lose the backup camera
issues.sym: The center touchscreen goes dark, so the backup camera image doesn't show when in reverse.
issues.why: A software problem could blank the center display. Acura recalled these SUVs for an update.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 25V032. Back up with extra care using mirrors until it is fixed.
